tracks.label: Power Electronics
tracks.description: Power electronics covers converting, controlling, and conditioning electric power with solid-state devices — inverters, converters, and motor drives that move power between forms (AC/DC, high/low voltage) with minimal loss. It overlaps closely with power systems engineering, which deals with generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across the grid, including integrating renewable sources like solar and wind.
tracks.careers: Power electronics engineer, power systems/grid engineer, renewable energy engineer, EV powertrain engineer. Employers: utilities, EV/battery makers, renewable energy companies, industrial motor drive manufacturers, aerospace power systems.

tracks.label: Semiconductor Devices & Microsystems
tracks.description: This area studies the physics and fabrication of semiconductor devices (transistors, diodes) and MEMS — tiny mechanical sensors and actuators built with chip-fabrication techniques. It underlies nearly every modern electronic device, from a phone's accelerometer to the transistors on a CPU.
tracks.careers: Device/process engineer, IC design engineer, MEMS/sensor engineer, semiconductor fab process engineer. Employers: chipmakers, sensor manufacturers, consumer electronics companies, research labs.

tracks.label: RF & Communications
tracks.description: RF (radio frequency) and communications engineering designs the circuits and systems that transmit and receive information wirelessly — antennas, amplifiers, and mixers, plus the modulation/coding schemes used in cellular, Wi-Fi, satellite, and radar systems.
tracks.careers: RF engineer, wireless systems engineer, antenna design engineer, communications systems engineer. Employers: telecom companies, satellite/aerospace firms, defense contractors, chipmakers building wireless radios.

tracks.label: Signal & Image Processing
tracks.description: Signal and image processing focuses on algorithms that analyze, filter, compress, and extract information from signals — audio, sensor data, or images/video — often implemented in real time on embedded hardware or GPUs.
tracks.careers: DSP engineer, computer vision engineer, algorithms/ML engineer, audio engineer. Employers: consumer electronics, medical imaging, autonomous vehicles, camera/imaging tech, defense/radar.

tracks.label: Embedded & Digital Systems
tracks.description: Embedded and digital systems engineering designs the digital logic, microprocessors, and firmware that control everything from appliances to industrial machinery — using hardware description languages (HDLs) to design custom digital circuits (FPGAs/ASICs) and writing low-level software that runs directly on hardware.
tracks.careers: Embedded systems engineer, firmware engineer, FPGA/ASIC design engineer, digital design engineer. Employers: consumer electronics, automotive, industrial automation, IoT device makers, chip design companies.

tracks.label: Biomedical Instrumentation
tracks.description: Biomedical instrumentation applies electrical engineering to medical devices — designing the sensors, signal-conditioning circuits, and systems used in equipment like ECG/EEG monitors, ultrasound machines, and implantable devices.
tracks.careers: Biomedical/clinical engineer, medical device design engineer, R&D engineer at a medtech company, regulatory/quality engineer. Employers: medical device companies, hospital biomedical engineering departments, medtech startups.

courses.title: Pre-Calculus I
courses.description: Explores how numbers can be used to inform decisions about everyday life. Investigates numerical concepts, graphical displays, proportional relationships, equations, functions, and linear, exponential and other mathematical models.

courses.title: Pre-Calculus II
courses.description: Introduces functions and their multiple representations. Explores linear, quadratic, polynomial, and rational functions. Emphasis on conceptual understanding, application, and symbolic manipulation skill throughout the course.

courses.title: Pre-Calculus III
courses.description: Continuation of the study of functions. Explores exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions. Emphasis is placed on conceptual understanding, application, and symbolic manipulation skill throughout the course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Studies the development of differential calculus, starting with limits, continuity, and the definition of derivative. Emphasizes differentiation techniques and their applications.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration theory and techniques with applications in science and engineering.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Studies sequences and series, including convergence tests and Taylor polynomials and series, as well as the calculus of curves in the plane and space described in polar, parametric, or vector-valued form.

courses.title: Linear Algebra (Matrix Algebra)
courses.description: Introduces ordinary differential equations. Includes first- and second-order equations and Laplace transform.

courses.title: Matrix Algebra with Applications
courses.description: Introduces linear algebra, including systems of linear equations, Gaussian elimination, matrices and matrix algebra, vector spaces, subspaces of Euclidean space, linear independence, bases and dimension, orthogonality, eigenvectors, and eigenvalues. Applications include data fitting and the method of least squares.

courses.title: Advanced Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Introduction to the concepts and computation techniques of multivariable calculus, including partial derivatives, the chain rule, double and triple integrals, vector fields, line integrals, surface integrals, Green's Theorem, Stokes' Theorem, and the Divergence Theorem.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: Covers concepts of probability and statistics; conditional probability, independence, random variable, and distribution functions; descriptive statistics, transformations, sampling errors, confidence intervals, least squares, and maximum likelihood; and exploratory data analysis and interactive computing.

courses.title: Mechanics
courses.description: Basic principles of mechanics and experiments in mechanics for physical science and engineering majors.

courses.title: Electromagnetism and Oscillatory Motion
courses.description: Basic principles of electromagnetism, the mechanics of oscillatory motion, and experiments in these topics for physical science and engineering majors.

courses.title: Waves
courses.description: Electromagnetic waves, optics, waves in matter, and experiments in these topics for physical science and engineering majors.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: Covers atomic nature of matter, chemical reactions, stoichiometry, solution chemistry, atomic theory, chemical bonding, molecular geometry and structure.

courses.title: General Chemistry I Lab
courses.description: Laboratory experience designed to complement the knowledge gained in B CHEM 143. Emphasizes collection and analysis of laboratory results in a well prepared laboratory notebook.

courses.title: Programming I (C++ or Java)
courses.description: Introduces programming concepts within social, mathematical, and technological context. Topics include programming fundamentals (control structures, data types, functions, etc.), computer organization, algorithmic thinking, introductory software engineering concepts, and social and professional issues.

courses.title: Programming II (C++ or Java)
courses.description: Transition from basic programming skills to a rigorous process of software development. Familiarization with higher level programming techniques (recursion, generic programming, stacks, queues, trees, searching, and sorting).

courses.title: Data Structures, Algorithms, and Discrete Mathematics I
courses.offeredNote: Not sampled (only B EE quarterly schedules were sampled) — check MyPlan/Time Schedule.
courses.description: Integrating mathematical principles with detailed instruction in computer programming. Explores mathematical reasoning and discrete structures through object-oriented programming. Includes algorithm analysis, basic abstract data types, and data structures.

courses.title: Introduction to Embedded Systems
courses.offeredNote: Not sampled (only B EE quarterly schedules were sampled) — check MyPlan/Time Schedule.
courses.description: Introduction to the process of specifying and designing embedded systems. Follows the embedded systems development process: software and hardware partitioning, processor selection, real-time operating systems, coding in assembly language and C, debugging, and testing.

courses.title: Composition
courses.description: Offers an interdisciplinary approach to composition, including generating a compelling topic; the articulation of a thesis; the development of supporting evidence; the ability to draw conclusions from the evidence, clear organization of the essay, correct mechanics; awareness of audience, and knowledge of resources for research.

courses.title: Composition, Research, and Reasoning
courses.description: Strengthens performance of college-level argumentative writing and scholarly research, critical reading and thinking, and the critique and creation of print and new media texts.

courses.title: Technical Writing
courses.description: Explores the most effective methods of communication based on the common expectations for computing and other engineering professionals. Examines various writing patterns commonly used in technical writing, including compare/contrast, persuasive, process, instructions, and problem/solution, and when/why each is used.

courses.title: Engineering Design and Innovation
courses.offeredNote: Scheduled around the capstone cohort — check the Time Schedule / your advisor.
courses.description: This course prepares students of the Electrical/Computer/Mechanical Engineering programs to start capstone courses. Topics include engineering ethics; consideration of societal, environmental and other factors in design; innovation, design process, and methodology; human centered design; project planning and management; introduction to capstone projects.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Engineering I
courses.offeredNote: Scheduled around the capstone cohort — check the Time Schedule / your advisor.
courses.description: The first course of a two-sequence capstone design course where students work on real-world multidisciplinary engineering projects to design a system, component, or process with specific realistic design constraints such as cost, engineering standards, and social impact. In this first course, students are expected to define and formulate the design problem, study alternative solutions, and develop a design plan and methodology.

courses.title: Capstone Project in Engineering II
courses.offeredNote: Scheduled around the capstone cohort — check the Time Schedule / your advisor.
courses.description: The second course of a two-sequence capstone design course where students work on real-world multidisciplinary engineering projects to design a system, component, or process with specific realistic design constraints such as cost, engineering standards, and social impact. In this second course, students are expected to refine and complete, build, and test their design work with the direct supervision of an engineering faculty.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to electrical engineering. Basic circuit concepts. Mathematical models of components. Kirchhoff's laws. Resistors, sources, capacitors, inductors, and operational amplifiers.

courses.title: Electric Circuits Lab
courses.description: The laboratory course of electrical engineering with selected laboratory experiments emphasizing measurement, analysis, and fundamental laws of electric circuits.

courses.title: Circuit Theory
courses.description: Electric circuit theory. Analysis of circuits with sinusoidal signals. Phasors, system functions, and complex frequency. Frequency response. Computer analysis of electrical circuits. Power and energy. Two port network theory.

courses.title: Continuous Time Linear Systems
courses.description: Introduction to continuous time signal analysis. Basic signals including impulses, pulses, and unit steps. Periodic signals. Convolution of signals. Fourier series and transforms in discrete and continuous time. Computer laboratory.

courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
courses.description: Overview of digital computer systems. Digital logic, Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits and logic design, programmable logic devices, and the design and operation of digital computers.

courses.title: Devices and Circuits I
courses.description: Physics, characteristics, applications, analysis, and design of circuits using semiconductor diodes and field-effect transistors with an emphasis on large-signal behavior and digital logic circuits.

courses.title: Devices and Circuits II
courses.description: Examines the characteristics and models of bipolar and field-effect transistors, linear circuit applications, including low and high frequency analysis of differential amplifiers, current sources, gain stages and output stages, circuitry of op-amps.

courses.title: Discrete Time Linear Systems
courses.description: Discrete time signals and systems, impulse response, convolution, Z-transforms, discrete time Fourier analysis. Computer laboratory.

courses.title: Applied Electromagnetics
courses.description: Introductory electromagnetic field theory and Maxwell's equations in integral and differential forms; uniform plane waves in linear media; boundary conditions and reflection and transmission of waves; guided waves; transmission lines and Smith chart; and electrostatics.

courses.title: Microprocessor System Design
courses.description: Examines the specification and design of a microprocessor-based computer system dedicated to a specific application. Covers low-level programming, memory systems, I/O and system debugging.

courses.title: Introduction to Electric Power Generation
courses.description: Reviews the design and operation of power plants for the generation of electric power. Covers thermodynamic principles of energy conversion, cycle analysis, combustion, nuclear and hydroelectric power, emerging energy technologies, plant economics, emission controls, and environmental impact.

courses.title: Digital Communication
courses.description: Covers the basic principles and techniques of digital signal transmission and reception. Examines the process of converting analog signals to digital formats, explores various digital modulation schemes, analyzes the limitations imposed by noise on communication systems.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital System Design Using HDLs
courses.description: Modeling techniques with the Verilog hardware description language; methodologies for finite-state machine (FSM) design, register-transfer level (RTL) design, and datapath and control unit design; computer arithmetic algorithms; and fast arithmetic hardware architectures.

courses.title: Electronic Circuit Design
courses.description: Provides an understanding of modern analog solid-state circuit design techniques used for instrumentation purposes. Emphasizes design techniques using integrated circuits, particularly operational amplifiers.

courses.title: Biomedical Instrumentation I
courses.description: Introduction to the basic principles of medical electronic instruments. Covers biopotentials, biosignal amplifiers, electrical safety, the design of clinical electronics and FDA regulations.

courses.title: Biomedical Instrumentation II
courses.description: Introduction to the principles of measuring human vital signals such as blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate. Covers medical imaging techniques (CT, MRI, PET) and the working principles of clinical ultrasound systems.

courses.title: Electronic Test and Measurement
courses.description: Introduction to the principle of metrology and modern electronic testing and measurement. Topics covered include types of testing and design-for-testability techniques such as scan-path, boundary scan and built-in-self test.

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Examines methods and techniques of digital signal processing. Reviews sampling theorems, A/D and D/A converters, demodulation by quadrature sampling, Z-transform methods, linear shift-invariant systems, difference equations, signal flow graphs for digital networks.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Digital Image Processing
courses.description: Introduction to digital image processing emphasizing image processing techniques, image filtering design and its applications. Topics include mathematical foundations for digital manipulation of images; image pre-processing; spatial and frequency-domain filtering, morphological transformations and segmentation.

courses.title: Introduction to Control Systems
courses.description: Provides an introduction to analysis and design of control systems with applications ranging across electrical, mechanical, and electromechanical systems. Topics include system modeling, performance and stability analysis using root locus, Bode and Nyquist plots.

courses.title: Introduction to Power Electronics
courses.description: Introduction to power electronics. Topics covered include characterization of power semiconductor devices, design of magnetic components and filters, analysis and design of ac-to-dc, dc-to-dc and dc-to-ac power converters. Applications in power supplies are presented.

courses.title: Introduction to MEMS
courses.description: Develops the basics for microelectromechanical devices (MEMS) including micro-actuators, micro-sensors, and micro-motors, principles of operation, different micromachining techniques (surface and bulk micromachining), IC-derived microfabrication techniques, thin-film technologies.

courses.title: Introduction to RF and Microwave Engineering
courses.description: Theory of transmission lines and microwave network analysis techniques used to design passive microwave devices. Topics include operational properties of active microwave circuits, antennas, and electromagnetic waves. RF, microwave RADAR and remote sensing systems.

courses.title: Introduction to Electrical Machines and Drives
courses.description: Introduction to electrical machines and drives. Topics covered include principles and analyses of electromechanical systems including dc, synchronous and induction machines, both motors and generators. Control strategies for the different machine types are presented.

courses.title: Electrical/Power Electronic Systems in Renewable Energy
courses.description: Provides a quantitative and practical introduction to renewable energy electrical/power electronic systems. Emphasis on the fastest growing solar and wind technologies. Electrical/electronic architectures of other technologies such as hydroelectric power and electric vehicles are introduced.

courses.title: Power System Fundamentals
courses.description: Basic power system analytical concepts, three-phase systems, impedance, steady-state network analysis, normalization, transmission lines, transformers, and synchronous machines.

courses.title: Power System Analysis
courses.description: Topics include iteration and simulation techniques as well as numerical solutions required to analyze power and energy systems; power flow; symmetrical components; and faulted system analysis and stability study.

courses.title: Semiconductor Devices
courses.description: Covers fundamentals of semiconductor theory: carrier diffusion and drift; concept of direct and indirect energy gap materials, effective mass of mobile carriers; device physics; homo- and heterojunctions, metal-semiconductor junction, bipolar transistor, and MOS transistors.

courses.title: Sensors and Sensor Systems
courses.description: Focuses on understanding a broad variety of sensor technologies and their application as systems in everyday use. Provides both a foundation to move into a particular area of sensor technology and also a means to apply appropriate sensors for particular applications.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Integrated Circuit Technology
courses.description: Introduces the fundamentals of IC technologies. Covers the microelectronic processing technology, including evaporation, sputtering, epitaxial growth, diffusion, ion implantation, oxidation, chemical vapor deposition, and photoresists.

courses.title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
courses.offeredNote: Topic-dependent — content and availability vary by quarter.
courses.description: Explores special topics in electrical engineering.

courses.title: Independent Study in Electrical Engineering
courses.description: Independent study on a topic or area agreed upon by the instructor and student.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Electrical Engineering
courses.description: Undergraduate research on a topic agreed upon by the instructor and student.
